terms.comment: Cicero’s and Quintilian’s word for the part of philosophy that deals with argument (Greek λογική); also in the Greek form dialecticē. A logician is dialecticus. For the logic of a particular argument or plan, “its reasoning”, Latin says ratiō (see reason).

evidence: Cic. Off. 3.20: fōrmula Stōicōrum ratiōnī disciplīnaeque maximē cōnsentānea (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In agreement with something, fitting; ratiōnī cōnsentāneus is “logical”, and cōnsentāneum est “it is logical, it follows”.
Cicero writes the word in Greek letters (Fin. 1.22); in Latin letters it is late. dialectica is the classical word.

sources: Lewis & Short: dialecticus · Lewis & Short: consentaneus · Lewis & Short: logica
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. logic; logical.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 257.
